newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil real ends flat after Central Bank change.
newsitem.headline: Brazil real ends flat after Central Bank change.

text.p: Brazil's real closed flat at 1.0830 per dollar in calm trading in the commercial foreign exchange market after the nomination of Gustavo Franco as the new head of Brazil's Central Bank, dealers said.
The government announced on Tuesday that the president of Brazil's Central Bank, Gustavo Loyola, will resign and international affairs director Franco was nominated to replace him.
"The nomination of Gustavo Franco was seen by the market as a strong confirmation by the government of the current forex policy," one dealer for a foreign bank said.
Franco's appointment as Central Bank president must be confirmed by the Senate.

Dealers were forecasting a 0.1 percent decline in the reais-dollar mini-band on Thursday, because it will be the last day of the month and the Central Bank has changed the mini-band on this day for the last several months.
The current mini-band was set on July 25 at between 1.0820 and 1.0870 reais per dollar.
So far this month, the mini-band has fallen 0.51 percent against the dollar compared with monthly declines of between 0.57 and 0.61 percent in the past six months.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real closed at 1.0880 per dollar, down 0.02 percent. In the parallel market, the real rose 0.17 percent to end at 1.150 per dollar.
